item.title: Make listItems follow cursor pagination
item.brief: In inventory-client, change listItems(transport) so it resolves to every item in order by following next_cursor until it is null or absent. The first request sends no cursor; each later request passes the previous next_cursor back unchanged. Add tests with a fake transport covering multiple pages, a single page, and an absent next_cursor. Update the README to document that listItems follows pagination. Keep npm test passing. Commit the change.

pr.body: Approach: listItems loops over GET /items, sending no cursor first and then the previous next_cursor unchanged, until next_cursor is null or absent. It tracks every cursor seen and rejects a repeat, so a cycle cannot loop forever. It also rejects a response without an items array. Files: client.js, test/client.test.js (fake transport: multi-page with request sequence, single page with null cursor, single page with absent cursor, repeated cursor, cycle, missing items array), README.md. Checks: npm test 9/9 on 02449c2. The new multi-page and repeated-cursor tests fail on the base client.js. Assumptions: the server contract is taken from the brief; inventory-api was not touched or run here. Follow-up: README 'ordered by id' is pre-existing and not enforced by the client; it relies on the server order.
pr.summary: listItems now follows next_cursor across all pages. Now: returns every item in order, and rejects a repeated cursor. Before: returned only the first page.

item.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
item.brief: In inventory-api, change GET /items to cursor pagination exactly as the shared contract specifies: optional limit (1..100, default 20) and cursor query parameters; body {"items": [...], "next_cursor": string|null}; items ordered by id; 400 with {"error": "..."} for invalid limit or cursor. Add unit tests covering paging to the end, default limit, boundary limits, and invalid inputs. Update the README to document the new parameters and response. Keep python3 -m unittest passing. Commit the change.

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier

Added cursor pagination to GET /items in inventory-api on archon/zmeatt0y-add-cursor-pagination-to-get-items. Commits 0ac36f4 (feature) and c457ca2 (review fix); head c457ca2, tree f21536664d9dd0fa790953016c1c5f9dce834f3b. Follow-up, pre-existing and out of scope: get_item uses str.isdigit, so GET /items/² raises ValueError. No services were started. Review: pass.

pr.body: Approach: cursor is the id of the last item returned; the next page holds items with id greater than it. Parsing is in api.py (_parse_limit, _parse_cursor, _parse_digits) and raises BadRequest, which list_items turns into a 400. Digits must be ASCII, at most 18 significant digits, and non-strings are rejected. Files: api.py, test_api.py (12 tests: paging to end, default limit, boundary limits 1 and 100, exact fit, cursor past end, invalid limit and cursor including non-string values), README.md. Checks: python3 -m unittest, 12 OK on c457ca2. Review: whole-change pass at 0ac36f4 (review-1); blocking non-string bug from review-2 and review-3 fixed in c457ca2; delta pass on c457ca2 (review-delta). Assumptions: the cursor is an opaque decimal id; the default page size change is contract-mandated. Not done: inventory-client listItems (not in this worktree).
pr.summary: GET /items now pages with limit (1..100, default 20) and cursor. now returns {items, next_cursor} ordered by id; invalid limit or cursor gives 400. before: all 57 items, no next_cursor. now: first 20 items with next_cursor "20". Breaking for callers that expected the full list.

risk.why: Changes the default response of GET /items for existing callers (57 items becomes 20 plus a next_cursor key), which the stage rubric rates high as an API change that breaks callers. Touches api.py parsing and tests and README; no security, locking or migration. Review found and fixed one blocking input-validation bug. Reviewers agreed on high.
